chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from his father, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): Regarding a man who sets out on a journey, then it becomes apparent to him that he should stay (reside) while he is in his prayer, should he complete the prayer or shorten it? He said: 'He completes it if it becomes apparent to him that he should stay.'

key_terms.إِقَامَة: Residence or staying in one place, ending the state of travel
key_terms.يُتِمُّ: To complete the prayer (performing all four rak'at for Dhuhr, Asr, and Isha)
key_terms.يُقَصِّرُ: To shorten the prayer (performing two rak'at for Dhuhr, Asr, and Isha)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on shortening prayer if a traveler decides to stay in one place during the prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the transitional status of a traveler who decides to settle (*muqim*) mid-prayer, establishing that the intention to stay takes precedence for the remainder of the current prayer unit. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle that the change in legal status (*hukm*) occurs immediately upon the manifestation of the new intention, distinguishing it from cases where the decision is made before or after the prayer. It serves as a foundational precedent for understanding how dynamic changes in a believer's state affect ritual obligations in real-time.
